title: Free-insertion comparison detects exceptional quotient mates
statement:
Fix $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $R$, a uniformizer $\varpi$ and $A_n=R/\varpi^n$ for $n\ge1$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $f:X\to Y$ be separated finite type between separated finite-type $k$-schemes [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties], with compactification $X\xrightarrow{j}\overline X\xrightarrow{p}Y$ [def-weil-compactifications-refinements]. For $W=X,Y,\overline X$ and $\tau=\mathrm{et},\mathrm{proet}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site, def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], let $\mathscr S_W^\tau$ be the category of strict systems of $(A_n)_W$-module sheaves with semilinear quotient transitions and componentwise morphisms [lem-pur-coefficient-system-derived-comparison]; use its ordinary unbounded derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], exact evaluations $e_n$ and, for $m\ge n\ge1$, derived quotient functors $T^W_{m,n}=-\otimes^L_{A_m}A_n$ [def-weil-derived-tensor]. Write $t^M_{m,n}:T^W_{m,n}M_m\to M_n$ for the scalar-extension adjunct of the actual transition. 
Work on the etale sites. Put $F=Rp_{*,\bullet}j_{!,\bullet}$, and let $F\dashv G$ and $F_n\dashv G_n$ be the ordinary etale adjunctions [lem-pur-etale-coefficient-system-adjoint]. Use the canonical $e_nF\cong F_ne_n$ and invertible compact-support quotient comparisons $q_{m,n}:T^Y_{m,n}F_m\to F_nT^X_{m,n}$. Let $L_n^W\dashv e_n$ be derived free insertion [lem-pur-coefficient-evaluation-derived-left-adjoint]: $(L_nK)_r=K\otimes^L_{A_n}A_r$ for $r\le n$ and zero otherwise. Let $\sigma^W_{m,n}:L_n^WT^W_{m,n}\to L_m^W$ be the canonical truncation map. Define $a_n:L_n^YF_n\to FL_n^X$ as the $L_n^Y\dashv e_n$ transpose of $1_{F_n}=e_nFL_n^X$.
Then $a_n$ is invertible; at $r\le n$ its evaluation is $q_{n,r}$, and it satisfies
$$F(\sigma^X_{m,n})a_{n,T^X_{m,n}}=a_m\sigma^Y_{m,n,F_m}L_n^Y(q_{m,n}^{-1}).$$
The natural representing bijections
$$\operatorname{Hom}(K,e_nGN)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(FL_nK,N)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(F_nK,N_n)$$
fix a counit-compatible isomorphism $e_nG\cong G_ne_n$. Under precisely these identifications the evaluated unit and counit are those of $F_n\dashv G_n$, and
$$t^{GN}_{m,n}=G_n(t^N_{m,n})b_{m,n,N_m},\quad b_{m,n}=G_n(T^Y_{m,n}\epsilon_m)G_n(q_{m,n,G_m}^{-1})\eta_{n,T^X_{m,n}G_m}.$$
These formulas are unchanged under the unique counit-compatible change of the chosen right adjoints. Mates have the convention of [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate]. They are assertions about actual derived-system maps, for arbitrary unbounded inputs.

proof.text: Apply the Brown-construction statement with $O=R$ and $t=\varpi$. Its left extension $L_n$ is the one of the strict-system level-extension lemma; that lemma and the free-insertion lemma both give $L_n$ as the total left derived functor of the same strict free insertion, left adjoint to $e_n$, with the same evaluation formulas computed on flat-term K-flat representatives. Hence the unique unit-compatible isomorphism of left adjoints identifies the two, compatibly with these evaluation formulas, and we use it tacitly. On such a representative the unit $P\to P\otimes_{A_n}A_n$ of the free insertion adjunction is $x\mapsto x\otimes1$. Brown then gives an actual natural isomorphism $c_n:L_n^YF_n\xrightarrow{\sim}FL_n^X$, namely the inverse of its displayed $FL_n^X\cong L_n^YF_n$; for $r\le n$, $e_rc_n=q_{n,r}$. The identity-ring clause of the coefficient-projection theorem gives $q_{n,n}=1$ under tensor-unit identifications. Thus $e_nc_n=1_{F_n}$. The unit of $L_n^Y\dashv e_n$ is the identity under $e_nL_n^Y=1$, by its explicit free-insertion formula. Consequently the adjunction bijection sends $c_n$ to $1_{F_n}$, so its injectivity gives $c_n=a_n$. This proves invertibility and every requested evaluated component without constructing a derived-system map from a family of components. All four cited results apply to ordinary unbounded derived categories, and the Brown theorem permits the separated finite-type schemes in the statement.

proof.text: Fix $m\ge n$ and an object $K$ at coefficient level $m$. Both sides of the claimed truncation equation have source $L_n^YF_nT^X_{m,n}K$ and target $FL_m^XK$. Compare their adjuncts under $L_n^Y\dashv e_n$, rather than compare all evaluations. For the left side, $e_na_{n,TK}=1$, and the explicit truncation formula gives $e_n\sigma^X_{m,n,K}=1_{T^X_{m,n}K}$; the canonical natural evaluation comparison for $F$ therefore makes its adjunct $1_{F_nT^X_{m,n}K}$. For the right side, $e_nL_n^Y(q_{m,n,K}^{-1})=q_{m,n,K}^{-1}$, $e_n\sigma^Y_{m,n,F_mK}=1$, and Step 1 gives $e_na_{m,K}=q_{m,n,K}$. Its adjunct is $q_{m,n,K}\circ q_{m,n,K}^{-1}=1$. Injectivity of this single Hom adjunction proves the equation as an equality of actual derived-system maps. The calculation is natural in $K$.

proof.text: Use the evaluation-bound theorem with the given adjunction $F\dashv G$, the given finite adjunctions $F_n\dashv G_n$, and $t=\varpi$. Its hypotheses are precisely the canonical evaluation and left-extension comparisons supplied by the Brown theorem. Step 1 identified that left-extension comparison with the transpose-defined $a_n$. The theorem's representing bijection is therefore exactly the composite in the question: its middle arrow is precomposition by $a_n$, followed by $L_n^Y\dashv e_n$. It gives the natural isomorphism $\theta_n:e_nG\cong G_ne_n$ and identifies the evaluated counit and unit with $\epsilon_n$ and $\eta_n$ under these particular identifications. No amplitude hypothesis is used: that hypothesis is needed only for the last, cohomological-bound clause of the cited theorem.

proof.text:
The transition clause of the same evaluation-bound theorem now applies under exactly these $\theta_n$. It identifies the transition of the actual $GN$ with $G_n(t^N_{m,n})\circ b_{m,n,N_m}$, where $b$ is the $F_n\dashv G_n$ transpose of $T^Y_{m,n}\epsilon_m\circ q_{m,n,G_m}^{-1}$. By the specified mate convention, this transpose is
$$G_n(T^Y_{m,n}\epsilon_m)\circ G_n(q_{m,n,G_m}^{-1})\circ\eta_{n,T^X_{m,n}G_m},$$
which is the displayed formula. In particular this is the inherited transition of $G$, not a replacement transition assigned to its evaluated objects. The theorem states this transition identification on unbounded systems, including compatibility through three indices.

proof.text: Let $G'$ and $G_n'$ be other chosen right adjoints. The unique-right-adjoint theorem gives the unique counit-compatible isomorphisms $\gamma:G\cong G'$ and $\gamma_n:G_n\cong G_n'$, characterized by $\epsilon'F(\gamma)=\epsilon$ and $\epsilon_n'F_n(\gamma_n)=\epsilon_n$. Under the representing Hom bijections of Step 3, these counit equations identify the two maps on every Hom set, so $\theta_n'e_n\gamma=\gamma_ne_n\,\theta_n$. The mate convention characterizes $b$ as the unique transpose of its counit composite. Substituting the same counit equations in that composite therefore gives $b'\,T^X\gamma_m=\gamma_nT^Y\,b$. The transition formula of Step 4 is consequently preserved by these isomorphisms, and its unit identification is preserved too, since the unit is the transpose of the identity. This proves independence under the stipulated unique counit-compatible changes.
